source_text: Amolire te itaque cum tali Deo tuo de Ecclesiarum medio; non est ipse, cui Patriarchae, cui Prophetae, cui Apostoli crediderunt, in quo speravit et sperat Ecclesia primitivorum, quae conscripta est in caelis [n74] ; non est ipse quem credit iudicem rationabilis creatura; quem Spiritus Sanctus iuste iudicaturum esse denuntiat. Nemo prudentium, pro tali Domino suum umquam sanguinem fudisset; nec enim merebatur dilectionis affectum, ut suscipiendae pro se onus imponeret passionis. Postremo iste quem inducis, si esset uspiam, reus convinceretur esse, non deus; iudicandus a vero Deo meo, non iudicaturus pro Deo. Ut igitur prima fidei fundamenta cognoscas: noster Deus, Ecclesiae catholicae Deus, substantia nobis ignotus est, et ab aspectu similiter remotus; quem vidit nemo hominum, nec videre potest [n75] ; ut aeternus sine principio, ita sanctus iustusque sine vitio; omnipotentissimus, aequissimus, misericordissimus, innotescens solo splendore virtutum; factor omnium quae non erant, dispensator eorum quae sunt, examinator cunctorum qui et sunt et futuri sunt et fuerunt, in ultimo die; terram, caelum, et cuncta simul elementa moturus; excitator cinerum, et corporum restitutor; sed propter solam iustitiam, haec quae diximus, cuncta facturus.
pass_a_gloss: Move yourself away therefore with such a God of yours from the midst of the Churches; he is not the one to whom the Patriarchs, to whom the Prophets, to whom the Apostles believed, in whom has hoped and hopes the Church of the firstborn, which has been written in the heavens; he is not the one whom a rational creature believes a judge; whom the Holy Spirit announces will judge justly. No one of the prudent would ever have poured his blood for such a Lord; nor indeed did he deserve an affection of love, that he should impose the burden of a passion to be taken up for himself. Finally this one whom you bring in, if he were anywhere, would be convicted to be a defendant, not a god; to be judged by my true God, not about to judge for God. That you may therefore know the first foundations of faith: our God, the God of the catholic Church, is unknown to us in substance, and likewise remote from sight; whom no one of humans has seen, nor can see; as eternal without beginning, so holy and just without vice; most omnipotent, most equitable, most merciful, becoming known by the splendor of virtues alone; maker of all things which were not, dispenser of those which are, examiner of all who both are and will be and have been, on the last day; about to move earth, heaven, and all the elements together; raiser of ashes, and restorer of bodies; but on account of justice alone about to do all these things which we have said.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Away with you, then, and this God of yours from the midst of the churches! He is not the one in whom the patriarchs, prophets, and apostles believed, in whom the church of the firstborn enrolled in heaven has hoped and still hopes (Hebrews 12:23). He is not the one whom rational creatures believe to be their judge, whom the Holy Spirit declares will judge justly. No sensible person would ever have shed his blood for such a Lord. He would not deserve the affection of love that could place on anyone the burden of suffering for him. Finally, if the one you introduce existed anywhere, he would be proved a defendant, not a god: someone to be judged by my true God, not someone to judge in God's place.

Learn, then, the first foundations of faith. Our God, the God of the catholic Church, is unknown to us in his substance and likewise beyond our sight, “whom no human being has seen or can see” (1 Timothy 6:16). As he is eternal without beginning, so he is holy and just without fault: supremely powerful, supremely fair, supremely merciful, made known only by the radiance of his virtues. He is the maker of all that did not exist, the ruler of all that exists, and on the last day the examiner of all who exist, will exist, or have existed. He will shake earth, heaven, and all the elements together; he will raise the ashes and restore bodies. But everything we have named he will do for justice alone (compare Hebrews 12:26–27; John 5:28–29).

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.
